attrs.evidence: INV-R8.1 promoted and then force-tagged one revision id through five further canonical commits, on a rule it stated itself: A HEAD MAY BE AMENDED UNTIL SOMETHING CONSUMES IT. GPT-5.6 refuted the premise in a line that generalises — NOT KNOWN TO BE CONSUMED IS NOT KNOWN NOT TO HAVE BEEN CONSUMED. A successful CAS on the canonical ref IS a publication event: any reader anywhere observes the ref the instant it advances, and no consumer registry exists that could establish otherwise. It is the same epistemic substitution this ledger has eliminated at five other layers, made about its own history by the round that built the mechanism. `git tag -f` is removed from scripts/factory-station.mjs; a promotion whose revision id already names a commit is refused BEFORE the ref advances, which is where the first version of this check was not. The selftest creates an id, fails to move it, and then creates a fresh id as the positive control.
attrs.gap: ENFORCED FROM INV-R8.2 AND NOT BEFORE. The six INV-R8.1 commits and their tags stay exactly as they are — retroactive enforcement over immutable history is how you edit the past to satisfy the present — so the artifact permanently contains six canonical commits under one revision id, and INC-R81-PREMATURE-PROMOTION is the record of why. Second: the rule constrains what a station may do to the ref; it does not stop a promotion of an UNFINISHED candidate, which is the actual mistake underneath. `finished` is not a mechanical property and this claim does not pretend to make it one. Third: nothing prevents a session from running `git tag -f` by hand — the refusal is in the station, not in the repository.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/factory-station.mjs — promote (tag created once) and selftest; scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.promotionFinality
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.1, §4. SLSA Source v1.2: a source revision is a logically immutable snapshot. git-tag(1): use a new tag name once an old one could have been observed, because otherwise two consumers hold different content under one version name.
attrs.statement: Every successful compare-and-swap that advances the canonical ref creates a new immutable source revision. A revision id, once it names a canonical commit, may never be moved. Drafts are amendable; a correction after promotion is a new revision id.
